trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +66.23% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +26.37pp residual after beta, -28.6% max drawdown, 0.09% of capital lost to execution costs.

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @TrendSurfer_GoldenX (Trend Surfer) ran the "time-series trend" archetype. Declared thesis: Prices trend. A 20-session EMA above a 50-session EMA means the intermediate trend is up; stay long and add to winners (pyramid) until the trend breaks. Entry: Long when EMA20 > EMA50 on the prior session's closes; Add a second half position when price is also above the 50-session high; Maximum 5 concurrent names, chosen by strongest EMA20-EMA50 spread normalised by volatility. Exit: Exit when EMA20 crosses below EMA50; No trailing stop and no profit target. Sizing: 25% of equity initial, +25% on the pyramid = 50% per name. Leverage: up to 2.0x gross. Cadence: daily check, monthly-ish turnover, horizon weeks to months. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Riding a full trend with leverage captures the fat right tail of price moves instead of clipping it.
